output: {"objective":"Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of BTK-p.Arg28His (BTK, UniProt Q06187) and test it with one targeted computational test.","subject":{"gene":"BTK","variant_id":"BTK-p.Arg28His","accession":"Q06187","position":28,"reference_residue":"R","alternate_residue":"H","protein_change":"p.Arg28His"},"events":50,"current_favourite":"H1","hypotheses":[{"id":"H1","mechanism_class":"ligand_binding","starting_rank":1,"statement":"Agent-generated hypothesis: R28 sits in the Btk PH-domain inositol-phosphate pocket (UniProt binding site for Ins(1,3,4,5)P4), and the Arg-to-His change removes the positive charge and H-bond geometry needed to bind the phosphate head group of Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 or phosphoinositides, so PH-domain membrane recruitment and BTK activation are lost.","supports":["E1","E10","E18","E3","E4","E14"],"would_refute":"Ligand-bound experimental structures (e.g. 1B55 with 4IP) show residue 28 with no side-chain or backbone contact to the inositol phosphate, and a homology model or docked R28H structure keeps the ligand pose and contact energy within the wild-type range (no loss of contact or interaction energy at position 28).","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H2","mechanism_class":"stability_folding","starting_rank":2,"statement":"Agent-generated hypothesis: R28 is a conserved structural residue in the PH-domain beta-sandwich, and His substitution destabilises the local fold (strand 25-32 packing or salt bridges), lowering folded-state stability and cellular BTK levels rather than removing a specific ligand contact.","supports":["E12","E15","E16","E14","E20","E17","E11"],"would_refute":"Structure-based stability predictions (for example FoldX or Rosetta ddG on the AlphaFold model AF-Q06187-F1 and on 6TT2) give a ddG for R28H below about 1 kcal/mol with no buried salt bridge or hydrogen-bond loss at residue 28, and the local backbone and residue 25-32 strand geometry stay unchanged in an R28H model.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H3","mechanism_class":"protein_interaction","starting_rank":3,"statement":"Agent-generated hypothesis: R28 lies at a PH-domain surface that contributes to a dimer or oligomer interface stabilised by inositol phosphate (as reported for the E41K invisible dimer), so H28 disrupts the interface and blocks the transautophosphorylation-competent assembly of BTK.","supports":["E7","E2","E17"],"would_refute":"Crystal lattice and biological-assembly analysis of the PH-domain structures (1B55, 6TT2 and related entries) shows residue 28 buried within a monomer with no solvent-accessible surface contacting a second chain, and an in-silico docking or interface-energy analysis of the AlphaFold dimer shows no contribution from residue 28 to the interface.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"}],"results":[{"test_id":"T1","test_kind":"ligand_contact","summary":"Residue 28 lies within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in
